To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pub/sub is a viable approach for supporting multiplayer games and that there is a trade-off between the number of message types and the number of messages.

(1) the design that integrates the interest management functionality in the networking engine is the one with the best performance, (2) the content-based design is the one with worst performance, and (3) the design that uses a topic-based pub/sub middleware is the one with intermediate performance.

1) the pub/sub paradigm is a viable solution to the networking challenges of multiplayer games; 2) the pub/sub middleware should be designed with the specific characteristics of the application in mind; 3) pub/sub middleware that integrates application-specific functionality is more efficient than a generic middleware that is used as a black box; and 4) the pub/sub approach is a promising alternative to the client-server approach for multiplayer games.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and implementation of a MMOG networking middleware that is able to support the location-based semantics, the highly interactive nature of these games, and the loosely coupled interactions between the various components of a MMOG.
understanding the role of pub/sub in MMOG networking and with identifying the most appropriate pub/sub approach and design for these games.
the development of scalable, efficient and flexible networking middleware for massively multiplayer online games.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pub/sub-based designs are a viable and promising alternative for the networking engine of MMOGs.
the topic-based pub/sub design is the most suitable for MMOGs, as long as the network engine is not integrated into the game functionality.
there is no single best pub/sub approach for a MMOG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
content-based pub/sub approaches are more suitable for the MMOG networking middleware.
the pub/sub middleware can be a viable option for the networking of MMOGs.
the pub/sub approach is an excellent candidate for the design and implementation of a MMOG networking layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design and evaluation of pub/sub-driven MMOG networking engines is an intricate process that requires a careful consideration of the different pub/sub approaches and their integration into the MMOG networking engine.
pub/sub can be successfully used to build a scalable and low-latency networking engine for MMOGs.
the design choices for a MMOG network engine are highly application-specific and that there are no clear winners in this space.
